result.modelObserved: Opus 5 — exact model id `claude-opus-5[1m]`, the tier explicitly declared at spawn. Declared, not inherited.
result.strongestDefect: L-18 — the dock's "certified chrome ink" referent is read off `.glass-dock`, a node that paints nothing under Glass 7 (measured `rgba(0,0,0,0)` in both schemes; the paint is on the `.dock-plate` child, measured α 0.5392 light / 0.5776 dark). `resolveLiveTint` therefore returns `undefined` on every call and the static model it exists to distrust (α 0.80/0.88) serves every certification on the dock band, unnoticed since the W44 Glass 7 adoption. The mechanism is a demo feature module (`demo/color-session/useContrastSafeColor.ts:152`) reaching across two package boundaries into a producer-private DOM class by `document.querySelector` — the weakest coupling the language offers, for a value the producer already computes, serving exactly one consumer (`ProfileSection.vue:28`, the dock).
result.negativeProof: Verdict is DEFECTIVE, but three axes were checked and found sound and are recorded as such in the report: (1) no demo file reaches into `src/` or `dist/` — all 50 value.js import sites use published `package.json#exports` subpaths (`grep -rho '@mkbabb/value.js[a-z/]*' demo | sort | uniq -c` → 25 /color, 10 /css, 6 /math, 5 /easing, 4 /quantize, 1 bare inside a comment); Dock.vue imports the library not at all, correct for chrome. (2) `verbatimModuleSyntax` holds across the whole dock subtree, and it is load-bearing: because `Dock.vue:24`'s `import type { DockActionBar }` is erased, the dock's runtime graph is 65 modules rather than the 195 that `usePaneRouter` itself pulls (measured, L-graph2.mjs). (3) `main` = 1 and `nav` = 1 on 60/60 audit captures and live; the producer's inert/aria-hidden packaging of inactive dock faces is correct (measured `inert:true, visibility:hidden` at rest).

defects.defect: The chrome-tier ink referent probes a node that paints nothing: `resolveLiveTint("chrome")` reads `getComputedStyle(document.querySelector('.glass-dock')).backgroundColor`, which is fully transparent under Glass 7 — the glass is painted on the `.dock-plate` child. The live probe returns undefined on every call and the static model silently serves.
defects.evidence: demo/color-session/useContrastSafeColor.ts:150-153 (the querySelector) and :217 (`if (!resolved || resolved.alpha === 0) return undefined`). Measured live (scratchpad L-probe5.mjs, /#/, 1280x900, dock expanded): light {"dockBg":"rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)","plateBg":"color(srgb 0.931227 0.845921 0.816039 / 0.5392)"} ; dark {"dockBg":"rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)","plateBg":"color(srgb 0.390298 0.334077 0.29024 / 0.5776)"}. Producer paint site: node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/dock/styles/morph.css `.glass-dock:not(.vertical) .dock-plate { background: color-mix(...) }`. Static fallback now in force: demo/color-session/ink.ts:29-35 RUNG_ALPHA.floating = {light 0.8, dark 0.88}, FLOATING_TINT_L = {light 1, dark 0.345}, applied to chrome at ink.ts:118-122. Sole consumer of the tier: `grep -rn 'useSafeAccentFn("chrome")' demo` -> demo/shell/dock/menus/ProfileSection.vue:28.
defects.mechanism: Cross-package boundary violation: a demo feature module reaches a producer's internal paint value through a DOM class-name query instead of a published token/contract. Untyped, unexported, untested — so a producer paint change (Glass 7, adopted whole at V·W44) un-wires it silently.
defects.reproduction: node scratchpad/L-probe5.mjs against the live dev server on localhost:9000 — prints dockBg rgba(0,0,0,0) and the real plateBg with alpha 0.5392/0.5776 in light/dark. Consequence example (labelled: assumed ambient L 0.75): surfaceLightness = a*L + (1-a)*ambient gives 0.95 modelled vs 0.83 measured — ink certified against a surface an eighth of the OKLab range too light. e2e/smoke/oracles/o18-contrast-census.spec.ts:594-635 measures only the outcome at one boot colour and never asserts the live probe returned anything.
defects.proposedCure: The referent is the producer's own composited value, so the producer publishes it: glass-ui exposes `--glass-tint-chrome` (resolved) or `useDockSurfaceTint()` on the existing DockContext, and the demo reads a token, never a node. The `chrome` branch — and the identical `querySelector('[data-surface="veil"]')` idiom at :170-176 — then collapse to token reads with no DOM archaeology. Interim `.glass-dock .dock-plate` is another line of the same wrong kind and will break on the next paint change. Secondary: the selector is document-order dependent — two `.glass-dock` elements exist on /#/atmosphere and /#/blob (demo/scenes/ConfigSliderPane.vue:164); measured firstIsShell:true today, breakage on re-order is a hypothesis.

defects.defect: `isAdminMode` is a one-way latch defined by two disagreeing predicates. After one visit to a tuning route the dock wears admin identity (gold shimmer glyph + gold `--dock-ring`) on every subsequent non-admin route for the rest of the session.
defects.evidence: demo/shell/dock/composables/useDockAdminMode.ts:32 seeds the ref with a PREFIX test `currentView.startsWith("admin-")`; :55-59 maintains it with a MEMBERSHIP test `adminViews.includes(view)` and has no falsifying arm. The two predicates disagree on `atmosphere`/`blob` (in the array at :27, not prefixed). Reproduced live (scratchpad L-probe6.mjs, headless Chromium 1280x900): `1 fresh picker {"route":"#/","goldIcon":false,"ring":"oklch(0.471189 0.188448 9.8340"}` / `2 -> atmosphere {"goldIcon":true,"ring":"light-dark(oklch(0.751 0.147 8"}` / `3 back() -> picker {"route":"#/","goldIcon":true,"ring":"light-dark(oklch(0.751 0.147 8"}` / `4 -> palettes {"goldIcon":true,...}`.
defects.mechanism: Duplicated state for a value that is a pure function of the route, with the predicate implemented twice and neither copy owned by the schema that owns views (demo/shell/viewSchema.ts).
defects.reproduction: node scratchpad/L-probe6.mjs — load /#/ (gold false), hash to /#/atmosphere (gold true), page.goBack() to /#/ (gold STILL true), hash to /#/palettes (gold STILL true). With admin credentials the damage is functional, not cosmetic: viewEntries (:34-39) then returns only the seven admin views while on /#/palettes, so the dock's own navigation cannot reach the user views except through the `__admin_toggle__` sentinel row.
defects.proposedCure: Derive, do not latch. Add `group: "user" | "admin"` to `PaneConfig` (viewSchema.ts owns the partition) and reduce the composable to `const isAdminMode = computed(() => VIEW_MAP[viewManager.currentView.value].group === "admin")`. The ref, both watchers and both hardcoded ViewId arrays die; `toggleAdminMode` keeps its real job (it navigates) and the flag follows the route by construction — the same transposition `useViewManager.ts:51-58` already applied to `mobilePaneIndex`.

defects.defect: The local `useLayerTransition` shim in ActionBarLayer produces no crossfade at all: the producer CSS the template hand-binds declares no opacity transition, so the 260 ms timer window is an instant cut with a transparent inert box held over the live controls.
defects.evidence: demo/shell/dock/layers/ActionBarLayer.vue:62-94 (the shim, SUB_LAYER_CROSSFADE_MS = 260, subLayerProps hand-binding `.dock-layer`/`is-active`/`is-leaving`). Producer rules: node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/dock/styles/layers.css declares only `transition: visibility 0s linear var(--duration-normal)` on `.dock-layer`; the opacity overlap lives on `.dock-crossfade[data-crossfading] > .dock-face` via `--dock-t` (crossfade.css), reachable only inside `<DockCrossfade>`. Measured live (scratchpad L-probe2.mjs), both faces at rest / +60ms / +460ms across the actions->input swap: `transitionProperty: "visibility", transitionDuration: "0s"` at every phase; opacity steps 1->0 and 0->1 in one frame; the leaving face holds a 442x45 transparent inert box. The public successor exists: node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/dock/index.d.ts:5 `export { default as DockCrossfade } from "./DockCrossfade.vue";` — contradicting the shim's own comment at ActionBarLayer.vue:54-61.
defects.mechanism: A local fork of a retired producer concept, styled out of the producer's private stylesheet by class-name convention; the fork reimplements the packaging but cannot reach the animation, which the producer moved behind a component.
defects.reproduction: node scratchpad/L-probe2.mjs — navigate /#/, click [aria-label='Toggle action bar'], click [aria-label='Open color input'], sample getComputedStyle on both children of `.dock-layer-grid` at 60 ms and 460 ms. transition-property is `visibility` and duration `0s` in all four phases.
defects.proposedCure: Replace ActionBarLayer.vue:62-101 with `<DockCrossfade :active="activeSubLayer" reserve="inline">` wrapping two `<DockLayer id="actions">` / `<DockLayer id="input">` faces. The shim, the 260 ms literal, the timer, `subLayerProps`, `subLayerGridEl`, the `void opts.containerEl` parity argument and the hand-bound producer classes all die (~40 lines), and the producer's spring-driven overlap, peak-size reserve and focus transfer from a dissolving face arrive instead of being approximated.

Extend the existing owner rather than adding one: `useDocumentTitle` becomes `useDocumentIdentity(route)` returning `{ title, heading }` from the same `viewSchema` row, the shell renders `

{{ heading }}

` as the first child of App.vue's `

defects.defect: The demo's declared view of the published library surface has drifted from `package.json#exports`: tsconfig.demo.json maps a nonexistent `dist/index.d.ts`, declares two subpaths that are not exported, and omits two that are — while calling itself a mirror of the generated Vite alias set.
defects.evidence: `package.json#exports` keys = ['./color','./value','./css','./easing','./math','./transform','./quantize'] — 7 keys, no '.' root. tsconfig.demo.json paths declare `@mkbabb/value.js` -> ./dist/index.d.ts (`ls dist/index*` -> no matches found), plus `/parsing` and `/units` (neither in exports; no src/subpaths/parsing.ts or units.ts — `ls src/subpaths` -> color, css, easing, math, quantize, transform, value), and omit `/value` and `/css` (both exported; `/css` used 10x in demo and 4x inside glass-ui's dist). The file's header calls this 'the 8 public keys' / 'a CLOSED 8-key set' that 'mirrors the vite.config.ts runtime self-alias generated from the same map'; vite.config.ts:41-50 generates one alias per exports entry -> 7 aliases and no bare-root alias.
defects.mechanism: A hand-maintained declaration of a generated surface: the runtime alias set is derived from exports, the type paths are not, so the two views of the public API drift silently.
defects.reproduction: NONE — latent, not live. No demo file imports the bare `@mkbabb/value.js` specifier (`grep -rn '@mkbabb/value.js"' demo` -> the only hit is prose at demo/shared/utils.ts:12), and glass-ui's three specifiers (/color, /css, /easing, measured in its dist) are all covered by the generated alias set, so one instance serves the running app. Were the bare specifier ever written it would resolve to node_modules/@mkbabb/value.js@4.0.0 — the published copy npm installed for glass-ui's peer dep — a second instance of this library behind an undeclared specifier.
defects.proposedCure: Generate the tsconfig `paths` from `package.json#exports` exactly as the Vite aliases already are (one loader, one source of truth), or add a real `"."` export plus `dist/index.d.ts`. Either way the two declarations of the public surface cannot drift apart again — this is the axis T.W1's dogfood keystone was fought over.

result.axis: CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, design-system boundary, proportion/seat law) for demo/shell/dock/ColorInput.vue
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 (claude-opus-5[1m], 1M context) — the tier explicitly declared at spawn; seat declared, not inherited.
result.strongestDefect: D-1 — the only focus indicator on the app's primary text-entry control is `border-color: <the user's own selected colour, alpha included>` with the UA outline explicitly suppressed (`focus-visible:outline-none`, ColorInput.vue:16 + :162-166). Measured contrast against the field's own background rgb(251,250,248): #fbfaf8 → 1.00:1; white → 1.04:1; alpha 0 → fully transparent. WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.11 floor is 3:1. There is no forced-colors fallback either — the element matches NONE of foundation.css:702-720's focus-restoration roster (measured el.matches(roster) === false; role="textbox"/[contenteditable] are not in the roster and the element carries no tabindex attribute). And in the error state the destructive branch of `inputStyle` returns first, so the error border erases the focus border entirely. The bitter part: the app's certified contrast-safe accent (SAFE_ACCENT_KEY, computed from cssColorOpaque precisely so alpha cannot destroy contrast) IS injected in this same component at :157 — and is spent on the arrow glyph's stroke while the raw alpha-bearing cssColor takes the focus indicator.

defects.defect: Focus indicator is the user's raw alpha-bearing colour with the UA outline suppressed; measured contrast 1.00:1 for reachable colours; no forced-colors fallback; error state overwrites focus state.
defects.evidence: demo/shell/dock/ColorInput.vue:16 (`focus-visible:outline-none`) and :162-166 (`if (inputIsFocused.value) return { borderColor: cssColor.value }`). Live after a real click: `focused: true, outline: "none 1px rgb(0,95,204)", inlineStyle: "border-color: lab(92 88.8 20 / 0.827);"`. Measured contrast vs the field's own measured background rgb(251,250,248): `#fbfaf8` → 1.00, `rgb(255 255 255)` → 1.04, `oklch(0.7 0.1 200 / 0)` → alpha 0 / invisible. Forced-colors roster membership measured via el.matches() against foundation.css:702-720: colorInput → false, sendBtn → true; colorInput attrs = [data-v-…, contenteditable, role, aria-label, class] (no tabindex). Error+focus measured inline style: `border-color: var(--destructive)`. Contrast-safe primitive available and unused for this purpose: demo/color-session/useContrastSafeColor.ts:273-292, injected at ColorInput.vue:157 and spent on the arrow stroke at :74/:81.
defects.mechanism: Accessibility-critical state expressed through a user-data-driven decorative channel with no floor, no fallback register, and no separation from a competing state — instead of a design-system focus register.
defects.reproduction: http://localhost:9000/#/ at >=1440px viewport → hover the dock → click `Tools` (aria-label="Toggle action bar") → click `Open color input` → drag the alpha channel slider to 0 (or set the colour to white in light mode) → click the field. Focus is undetectable. In WHCM the element matches no outline-restoration selector.
defects.proposedCure: Delete `focus-visible:outline-none` and the focus branch of `inputStyle` entirely. Focus comes from the house register — demo/styles/focus-ring.css / the `.focus-ring` class that four sibling dock controls measurably carry (measured siblingButtonsUsingFocusRing: 4, colorInput.usesFocusRing: false). Architecturally this dissolves by adopting glass-ui `Input`, which owns its own focus register. If the live colour must appear on this control it appears as a swatch, never as the focus boundary.

defects.defect: The parse-error affordance carries zero programmatic semantics and physically occludes 83% of the send button and 66% of the field it describes.
defects.evidence: Measured with the badge live on screen (frames/B-error-badge-over-send.png): badge left 682.1 right 783.1 width 101.0; send left 763.1 right 787.1 width 24.0 → overlap 20.0px = 83% of the button; input width 153.0 → badge covers 66% of the field. defects.mechanism: An error rendered as a floating decoration positioned against the same physical edge as the recovery action, instead of as a field state with an associated message region.
defects.reproduction: Open the colour input at >=1440px, focus it, and drive a stream of distinct invalid strings at ~2.6s intervals (e.g. `lab(#)`, `lab(##)`, …) so the 2s auto-clear never fires. defects.defect: ~2.04s trailing debounce before any feedback, no live preview while typing at human cadence, and complete silence when the same invalid string is retried.
defects.evidence: demo/color-session/useColorParsing.ts:92 `debounce(parseAndSetColor, 2000)`; :62 `if (!input || input === previousInvalid) return;`; :57 error auto-clears after 2000ms. Four measured live trials — T1 fresh `lab()` → badge at 2037ms; T2 SAME `lab()` retried → badge NEVER; T3 different `zzz(` → 2048ms; T4 `lab()` again after previousInvalid changed → 2041ms. Separately: driving the field at a 900ms cadence for 4s produced no badge at all, because every keystroke resets the 2000ms trailing timer.
defects.mechanism: A trailing debounce an order of magnitude past the interaction-feedback threshold, combined with a stale-input dedup cache guarding a pure function, and an error truth that lives only on a 2s timer.
defects.reproduction: At http://localhost:9000/#/ with the colour input open and focused: type `lab()` and wait — the badge appears at ~2.04s and vanishes 2s later. Now clear and type `lab()` again — nothing ever appears. Separately, type `oklch(0.7 0.1 200)` at roughly one character per second: zero live colour preview for the entire 18-character entry.
defects.proposedCure: Leading-edge debounce at ~120-200ms for the live preview; derive the error state from the current value so it PERSISTS while the value is invalid rather than flashing on a timer; delete `previousInvalid` entirely — it is a cache guarding a pure function and it is the mechanism that silences the natural human retry loop. PROPORTION-AUDIT PR-08 already rules this family ADD-AFFORDANCE.

defects.defect: Direction and bidi: every offset is physical, and the field renders a CSS-colour string with no LTR isolation.

defects.defect: The crown entrance animation never runs, on any device, in any browser, and never has. ColorInput.vue:36-39 binds `animation: crown-appear ...` in an INLINE style attribute; ColorInput.vue:369-376 defines `@keyframes crown-appear` inside `<style scoped>`. Vue's SFC compiler hash-suffixes scoped keyframe names and rewrites animation declarations within the same style block, but does NOT process template style attributes. The inline reference resolves to nothing. NEW this pass — it also refutes the first pass's negative proof line 654, 'The animation law is honoured.'
defects.evidence: demo/shell/dock/ColorInput.vue:38 (inline `animation: crown-appear var(--duration-panel) var(--ease-decelerate) forwards;`) vs :369 (`@keyframes crown-appear`). Compiled sheet served by the dev server: `curl -s "http://localhost:9000/@fs/Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js/demo/shell/dock/ColorInput.vue?vue&type=style&index=0&scoped=55dadc03&lang.css"` → contains `@keyframes crown-appear-55dadc03 {...}` and, for contrast, the class-driven sibling correctly rewritten: `.color-input-mode-flash[data-v-55dadc03] { animation: input-mode-flash-55dadc03 ... }`. Live document keyframe census (all stylesheets, all CSSKeyframesRule names): {"exactCrownAppear": false, "crownLike": ["crown-appear-55dadc03"], "totalKeyframes": 54}. No global fallback: `grep -rn "crown-appear" demo/` returns exactly 3 hits — ColorInput.vue:38, ColorInput.vue:369, demo/DESIGN.md:213 (prose). demo/styles/animations.css does not contain it.
defects.mechanism: Wrong home for a keyframe, forced by a per-instance inline style. A scoped @keyframes is consumable only from a class rule in the same block; an inline style attribute is consumable only against a GLOBAL keyframe. Pairing the two is unsatisfiable by construction — no combination of the two halves can ever resolve. Violates edict 6 (an animation deleted by construction rather than by decision) and edict 5 (per-instance inline override where a root-level class belongs).
defects.reproduction: 1) `curl -s "http://localhost:9000/@fs/Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js/demo/shell/dock/ColorInput.vue?vue&type=style&index=0&scoped=55dadc03&lang.css"` — observe the definition is emitted as `crown-appear-55dadc03`. 2) In any live page at http://localhost:9000, evaluate: `[...document.styleSheets].flatMap(s=>{try{return [...s.cssRules]}catch{return []}}).filter(r=>r.type===CSSRule.KEYFRAMES_RULE).map(r=>r.name).includes('crown-appear')` → false.
defects.proposedCure: crown-appear is a design-language beat, not seat geometry: promote it to demo/styles/animations.css (which already exists and is the declared home for global keyframes) and drive it from a `.crown-badge` CLASS. The inline style attribute dies with it. Adopt the rule repo-wide: if the reference is inline, the keyframe must be global; if the keyframe is scoped, the reference must be a class in the same block. No third combination is legal.

The discriminant is erased at every hop. Two further silencers compound it: `initialParse` (useColorParsing.ts:83) suppresses a composable's first failure, and `previousInvalid` (useColorParsing.ts:62) makes any REPEAT of the same string a total no-op — the state a frustrated user reaches within two seconds.
